rubric.sample_method: 20 manually spaced comic numbers across all eight books, including first and last available numbered installments in this selection. Not a random sample or a best-of list.
rubric.quality: Unweighted sum of humor, character, visual storytelling, originality; each 1-5. Bronze 4-10; Silver 11-15; Gold 16-20.
rubric.adaptation: Separate 1-5 judgment of concrete new-project usefulness. Bronze 1-2; Silver 3; Gold 4-5. Not included in quality total.
guardrails: Do not score drawing polish as skill or artistic worth; visual storytelling means clarity, staging, rhythm and expressions.
Historical importance does not force a Gold quality rating.
Rate the visible installment, not an unread arc; do not penalize a continuation merely for being a continuation.
Missing transcript is a data-quality issue, not a comic-quality penalty.
No target distribution or forced medal quotas.
Adaptation pitches are new proposals, not claims about established canon.
Ratings are subjective editorial judgments pending creator calibration, not objective measurements.

reviews.title: The Funny Guy
reviews.review_basis: Full published page image and existing archive transcript; neighboring installments not reviewed
reviews.premise: The Ash misunderstanding turns into a literal volcanic launch.
reviews.strongest_moment: The deadpan deli-counter response gives the absurdity a human rhythm.
reviews.weakness: The finish depends heavily on a Pokemon catchphrase rather than a distinctive FG reversal.
reviews.adaptation_pitch: Keep as the origin exhibit; a volcanic launch could become a background callback.
reviews.review_note: The first comic has historical value independent of its editorial medal.

reviews.title: Gas
reviews.review_basis: Full published page image and existing archive transcript; neighboring installments not reviewed
reviews.premise: An atomic fart destroys the house, sending the cast toward Gas Town.
reviews.strongest_moment: The condemned-house notice treats the catastrophe as mundane civic business.
reviews.weakness: The town visit becomes a chain of incidents rather than one escalating payoff.
reviews.adaptation_pitch: Gas Town arena with unstable soda machines and launch hazards.
reviews.review_note: Several small labels are faint; the archive transcript contains only an exclamation.

reviews.title: Sunglasses So Cool They Kill You
reviews.review_basis: Full published page image and existing archive transcript; neighboring installments not reviewed
reviews.premise: A party, elevator, battle and lethal sunglasses compete for space.
reviews.strongest_moment: The advertised sunglasses immediately demonstrate their literal lethal promise.
reviews.weakness: The title gag arrives deep into a much longer sequence and is quickly abandoned.
reviews.adaptation_pitch: A dangerous sunglasses pickup whose benefit comes with a comic side effect.
reviews.review_note: Rate the whole page; the sunglasses sequence alone would score more strongly.

reviews.title: Repair Man
reviews.review_basis: Full published page image and existing archive transcript; neighboring installments not reviewed
reviews.premise: Repair Man survives an extended chain of humiliations, transformations and attacks.
reviews.strongest_moment: Swapping the grow/shrink labels gives the action an actual trick and reversal.
reviews.weakness: The page keeps adding incidents after several potential endings; some imagery relies on broad caricature.
reviews.adaptation_pitch: Repair Man gets unreliable size-changing tools and exaggerated recovery animations.
reviews.review_note: Specific movement and prop ideas are stronger than the overall pacing.

reviews.title: The Wish Tree
reviews.review_basis: Full published page image and existing archive transcript; neighboring installments not reviewed
reviews.premise: Repair Man repeatedly tries to destroy a wishing tree; FG eventually uses the obvious solution.
reviews.strongest_moment: A long physical defense ends with a matter-of-fact wish, making the earlier effort absurd.
reviews.weakness: The next-story setup dilutes what could have been a clean ending at the disappearing Repair Man.
reviews.adaptation_pitch: A wishing-tree objective that changes arena rules; defensive walls and tunneling are supporting mechanics.
reviews.review_note: The ending continues into another story; this score covers the visible page only.

reviews.title: Apple Grenades
reviews.review_basis: Full published page image and existing archive transcript; neighboring installments not reviewed
reviews.premise: Exploding fruit escalates into missiles, countermeasures, boosters and a transformation.
reviews.strongest_moment: The apple lands in the open mouth immediately after the target boasts about being missed.
reviews.weakness: After the opening payoff, much of the page is escalation without a second equally sharp joke.
reviews.adaptation_pitch: Apple-grenade pickup, counter-projectiles, and a transformation that unlocks air recovery.
reviews.review_note: The transformation and weapon silhouettes provide unusually direct game references.

reviews.title: Recycling
reviews.review_basis: Full published page image and existing archive transcript; neighboring installments not reviewed
reviews.premise: A stolen sandwich gives way to a long boss fight and a victory.
reviews.strongest_moment: The opening theft and stretched mouth communicate without much dialogue.
reviews.weakness: The title, sandwich opening and boss battle do not form a clear comic payoff on this page.
reviews.adaptation_pitch: Use selected recoil, projectile and knockback poses as combat-animation references.
reviews.review_note: Bronze for the complete comic does not mean the action drawings have no use.

reviews.title: Food
reviews.review_basis: Full published page image and existing archive transcript; neighboring installments not reviewed
reviews.premise: A cooking sequence moves from a song through pizza, other dishes and a final feast.
reviews.strongest_moment: Junior eating the cheese supplies a character interruption within the cooking process.
reviews.weakness: Preparation occupies most of the page, while the feast ends without a strong reversal.
reviews.adaptation_pitch: Kitchen intermission or food pickups; keep Junior stealing ingredients.
reviews.review_note: The opening is explicitly credited musical material; the rating favors the original cooking business.

reviews.title: ...And We're Back!
reviews.review_basis: Full published page image and existing archive transcript; neighboring installments not reviewed
reviews.premise: A variety-show sequence features Totally Bob and deliberately bad audience participation.
reviews.strongest_moment: Bob recounts a completely uneventful story and still receives enthusiastic applause.
reviews.weakness: Several unrelated sketches and the packing transition weaken the page as a single unit.
reviews.adaptation_pitch: Totally Bob as a deadpan announcer or a short animated sketch.
reviews.review_note: The anti-joke is a stronger adaptation candidate than the entire page.

reviews.title: Target Priority
reviews.review_basis: Full published page image and existing archive transcript; neighboring installments not reviewed
reviews.premise: Repair Man launches into a ship battle before the heroes board a surviving vessel.
reviews.strongest_moment: The giant beam and tiptoeing boarding party offer a useful contrast in scale.
reviews.weakness: Combat progression carries the page; the humor and standalone conclusion are comparatively slight.
reviews.adaptation_pitch: A ship stage that switches from exterior cannon fire to interior close combat.
reviews.review_note: Faint pencil and crowded speech lower confidence in minor wording; the action is clear.

reviews.title: Yield to Spedestrians
reviews.review_basis: Full published page image and existing archive transcript; neighboring installments not reviewed
reviews.premise: A vehicle outing ends with an injured Junior repaired using glue and bandages.
reviews.strongest_moment: The improvised repair is followed by the belated suggestion to seek a professional.
reviews.weakness: The opening detour delays the stronger accident-and-repair sequence.
reviews.adaptation_pitch: A slapstick repair/reassembly animation or a vehicle-hazard stage.
reviews.review_note: The title and contemporary reference are era-specific; evaluate the actual repair gag separately.

reviews.title: Private Ship
reviews.review_basis: Full published page image and existing archive transcript; neighboring installments not reviewed
reviews.premise: A sinking-ship captain dodge leads into an extended musical parody and a game session.
reviews.strongest_moment: The captain hands over his title to escape his own obligation.
reviews.weakness: That reversal is quickly displaced by borrowed entertainment and a transition to another installment.
reviews.adaptation_pitch: A captain-role hot-potato minigame; the ship is a possible arena setting.
reviews.review_note: The song sequence is discussed without reproducing its lyrics.

reviews.title: Do-Re-Mini-Mi
reviews.review_basis: Full published page image and existing archive transcript; neighboring installments not reviewed
reviews.premise: A chocolate-powered Mini-Mi turns a candy-shop trip into a handler-versus-monster routine.
reviews.strongest_moment: Repair Man blames the bargain leash as the creature becomes uncontrollable.
reviews.weakness: Some chase beats could be shortened so the chocolate trigger and final escape read faster.
reviews.adaptation_pitch: Mini-Mi has a chocolate resource, bite attacks and an unreliable leash/grapple mechanic.
reviews.review_note: Gold for a clear character-driven escalation, even though the story continues.

reviews.title: Space Wars
reviews.review_basis: Full published page image and existing archive transcript; neighboring installments not reviewed
reviews.premise: A space encounter becomes a succession of aerial, sword and robot exchanges.
reviews.strongest_moment: The move from ship wreckage into close combat gives the fight varied silhouettes.
reviews.weakness: The strip is primarily connective action; it lacks a distinctive payoff within this installment.
reviews.adaptation_pitch: A combat reference board for deflections, aerial attacks and giant-robot hazards.
reviews.review_note: A standalone editorial score is not a judgment on the full surrounding story arc.

reviews.title: Funny Girl
reviews.review_basis: Full published page image and existing archive transcript; neighboring installments not reviewed
reviews.premise: A sea arrival and trapped treasure introduce Funny Girl before an immediate family sparring match.
reviews.strongest_moment: The final whip exchange establishes her capability through action rather than a biography.
reviews.weakness: The long-lost-sister revelation arrives abruptly and receives little emotional or comic development.
reviews.adaptation_pitch: Funny Girl as a whip/reach fighter; a temple stage with treasure-triggered boulders.
reviews.review_note: Strong roster discovery. Relationship details need surrounding-story review before canon consolidation.

reviews.title: The Mall Haul
reviews.review_basis: Full published page image and existing archive transcript; neighboring installments not reviewed
reviews.premise: A shopping trip escalates through an aquarium incident into an unstoppable sales pitch.
reviews.strongest_moment: The salesman continues the same question through increasingly drastic attempts to stop him.
reviews.weakness: Some early shopping business can be trimmed to get to the repeating-salesman sequence sooner.
reviews.adaptation_pitch: A mall stage with a persistent salesman hazard, or a self-contained animated short.
reviews.review_note: The repeated line becomes the organizing joke, giving the chaos a clear structure.

reviews.title: Slop Buffet
reviews.review_basis: Full published page image and existing archive transcript; neighboring installments not reviewed
reviews.premise: A buffet order becomes a food fight, an RPG-style team action and a disastrous identity reveal.
reviews.strongest_moment: Target summons Junior, whose butter attack literalizes the battle-command format.
reviews.weakness: The late reveal adds a new joke direction after the food fight has already established a strong premise.
reviews.adaptation_pitch: Junior assist attack, butter ammunition, and a restaurant arena with escalating food hazards.
reviews.review_note: Excellent combat material; the full page is less focused than its strongest middle sequence.

reviews.title: The Hobo Revolt
reviews.review_basis: Full published page image and existing archive transcript; neighboring installments not reviewed
reviews.premise: An attack on the FG house meets excessive defenses while Junior struggles with a text adventure.
reviews.strongest_moment: The supposedly simple text game traps Junior in a repeated failed flask command.
reviews.weakness: The political framing is thin; the sharper joke is the contrast between the emergency and Junior's distraction.
reviews.adaptation_pitch: A home-defense arena with an absurdly excessive satellite special; Junior has a distracted idle gag.
reviews.review_note: The text-adventure joke uses recognizable existing comedy vocabulary, so originality is moderated.

reviews.title: The Russian Bear Factory
reviews.review_basis: Full published page image and existing archive transcript; neighboring installments not reviewed
reviews.premise: Target dismisses Junior's obvious destination, then presents that same discovery as his own.
reviews.strongest_moment: Junior's flat response exposes the confident leader's incompetence without stopping the scene.
reviews.weakness: The assembled-bear reveal is a setup for the next installment, rather than a complete final payoff.
reviews.adaptation_pitch: An assembly-line bear-factory stage, with the sign gag retained in a brief opening scene.
reviews.review_note: The Target/Junior dynamic is stronger than the borrowed brand-parody premise.

reviews.title: Theme Park
reviews.review_basis: Full published page image and existing archive transcript; neighboring installments not reviewed
reviews.premise: A supposed theme-park rescue becomes a fighting arena, with both teams introduced before battle.
reviews.strongest_moment: FG admits the rescue may just be something to do; the roster then gets individualized introductions.
reviews.weakness: The theme-park premise is abandoned quickly, and introductions occupy more space than the actual fight.
reviews.adaptation_pitch: Use as the primary FG Fighter roster/introduction reference; prototype Razor's spike-cannon exchange.
reviews.review_note: Gold adaptation value does not automatically make the whole comic Gold. The page ends mid-battle.
